title: Why Do Nails on a CHALKBOARD Make You Cringe? 😖
description:
You drag your nails down a chalkboard and your whole body cringes. Your own ear is making that screech louder: the nasty part of it sits in one narrow band of pitch, about 2,000 to 4,000 hertz, and your ear canal is a little tube that boosts exactly that band. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

How we know: in a 2011 experiment, taking that band out of the recording made the sound much less unpleasant. And in brain scans of 13 volunteers (2012), the more people hated a sound, the more the brain's alarm centre, the amygdala, turned the hearing area up. Why that band? Nobody is sure. It is the band our ears are most sensitive to, and it is also where screams sit. The weird part: people who were told the screech came from a piece of modern music rated it as less awful, but their skin reacted just the same. The old idea that it sounds like a monkey's alarm call did not hold up: in a 2004 test, monkeys reacted to it no more than to plain noise.
